learning.title: A claim about wiring cannot be proven by testing the things being wired
learning.trigger: A route, handler or job is mounted, registered or connected to middleware. Unit tests of the handler pass, and tenancy/auth tests of the handler pass, so the change looks proven.
learning.rule: Wiring is a property of the composition, not of the parts, so only a request through the real router (or a real dispatch through the real registry) can prove it. Verified 2026-11-17: the blob routes were mounted without the session middleware, so every call 403'd as anonymous - unit tests green, tenancy tests green, routes unreachable. The general shape: when the change is 'X is now connected to Y', the proof must exercise the connection, not X and not Y. For routes that means one request through the actual router asserting the authenticated path succeeds; for jobs, one dispatch through the real registry. A test that constructs the handler directly bypasses exactly the layer under test.

The composition proof must use an event the SYSTEM produces, not one you construct. Hand-building the payload and calling the workflow/handler directly re-creates the handler-directly problem one layer up: it proves the workflow handles that payload, not that the platform routes that event to that workflow. 'One dispatch through the real registry' is only a proof if the dispatch is real too. Verified 2026-11-17: a real PR body edit minted run 43992675635 at the same head as the push run 43992666952 but on a different route, which is what makes it a mapping proof rather than two samples of the same thing.

A composition-root test must assert the SUCCESS state or a SPECIFIC error code, never merely that something was refused. A test that asserts 'this is refused' can pass for the wrong refusal, which is a distinct failure mode from unproven wiring: not 'the connection is untested' but 'the test would accept a different failure as proof of the intended one'. Verified 2026-11-17 on #514: removing app.use("/v1/blobs/*", session) left 1 of 3 cases passing - the digest-mismatch case asserts 422, and an anonymous 403 is also a refusal, so it passed without any auth. The happy path and the replay case are what actually pin the middleware. Cheap check: red-prove the line and look at WHICH cases fail; if all of them fail you learn less than if one survives.

verification.requirement: If the diff changes mounting, registration, middleware order or a registry entry, at least one test must go through the real composition root (router/registry), not the handler in isolation. Name that test in the PR evidence.
